title: The Shifted Batch
brief: A customer of Meridian Works reports that ten brackets from delivered batch {{batch}} failed a fit check at assembly. You are the internal auditor asked to trace the batch through the records. You have 12 visit points to trace batch {{batch}} and decide how far the problem extends before the containment meeting.

actions.label: Pack-out records for the last two batches
General condition of the area
actions.note: Nothing of note for the purpose of this visit.

actions.label: A staff member: anything else to mention
actions.note: The staff member has nothing further to add on this topic.

actions.label: Older records for this area
actions.note: The older records show nothing relevant to this visit.

actions.label: How drawing revisions reach the cell
Notices and signs in the area
actions.note: The notices are current and not relevant to this visit.

evidence.text: Traveler for batch {{batch}} lists material lot M-208, machine 3, and caliper CAL-12. The setup sheet reference is signed by the setter.
variants: The traveler for batch {{batch}} records material lot M-208, machine 3, and caliper CAL-12, with a signed setup reference.
evidence.whyItMatters: Identification on the traveler lets the organization trace a batch to its material, machine, and instruments. Here the traveler is complete, and it is the key to the other records.
evidence.missedExplanation: The traveler is the map for the whole trail. Reading it first shows which instrument and machine to check next.
evidence.falseFindingNote: A complete, signed traveler is conforming. Its value is in the leads it gives you.

evidence.text: Receiving log: the material certificate for lot M-208 matches purchase order 7716 and is filed with the delivery note.
evidence.whyItMatters: Bought-in material is checked against the order before use. The check is recorded, so the material is not a cause here.
evidence.missedExplanation: Confirming that the material is conforming narrows the investigation to the cell and the instruments.
evidence.falseFindingNote: The certificate matches the order and is filed. This is evidence of control, not a problem.

evidence.text: Machine 3 setup sheet cites drawing revision B. The document system shows revision C was released nine days before batch {{batch}} started.
variants: The setup sheet at machine 3 refers to drawing revision B, although the document system released revision C nine days before batch {{batch}} began.
evidence.whyItMatters: People at the point of use must work from the current approved version of a document. An obsolete drawing at the machine can produce parts to the wrong requirement.
evidence.missedExplanation: The setup sheet revision is easy to read past. Compare every revision letter at the point of use with the document system.

evidence.text: Calibration record: caliper CAL-12 was due for calibration 11 days before batch {{batch}} was completed. No extension or verification is recorded.
evidence.whyItMatters: Measurements are only trustworthy when the instrument is calibrated or verified at the set interval. Results taken with an overdue instrument cannot be relied on, and earlier results need review.
evidence.missedExplanation: This card is often missed because it needs the instrument identity from the traveler. Note every instrument number on a traveler and check its status.

evidence.text: Pack-out record: pallet {{pallet}} holds parts from batches {{batch}} and {{batch2}}. There is no separation label between the batches.
variants: The pack-out sheet shows batches {{batch}} and {{batch2}} loaded together on pallet {{pallet}} with no label separating them.
evidence.whyItMatters: Outputs must stay identified so that an affected batch can be found and held. A mixed pallet widens the population that must be reviewed.
evidence.missedExplanation: Pack-out records show where parts went. When a batch is shared with another, the scope of containment grows.

evidence.text: Nonconformance log entry NC-0193: spindle drift on machine 3, opened six days before the complaint. No containment is recorded.
evidence.whyItMatters: When a process problem is known, its output must be identified and controlled so that it is not delivered by mistake.
evidence.missedExplanation: Open nonconformance records are a quick way to find known problems. Check what was done with the output while the record was open.

evidence.text: Cell supervisor: "We keep running revision B until the old stock is used up. Nobody told us to stop." (interview note 14)
evidence.whyItMatters: This statement confirms that an obsolete revision is used on purpose and that the release of revision C was not managed as a change at the cell.
evidence.missedExplanation: Interviews often confirm what a record suggests. Ask how documents and changes reach the point of use.

evidence.text: Coolant log shows one corrected entry: a single line through the error, the initials of the operator, and the date.
evidence.whyItMatters: A correction that leaves the original entry readable, with initials and date, is a sound way to correct a record.
evidence.missedExplanation: Not applicable: this card is conforming.
evidence.falseFindingNote: A properly corrected record is conforming. Reporting it as a nonconformity lowers precision.

evidence.text: A handwritten note on machine 3 reads "check Z offset". The operator explains that it repeats step 6 of the current work instruction WI-31.
evidence.whyItMatters: Informal notes are acceptable when they agree with the current instruction and do not replace it.
evidence.missedExplanation: Not applicable: this card is conforming.
evidence.falseFindingNote: The note matches the current instruction. An unusual-looking note is not a nonconformity by itself.

evidence.text: Final inspection record for batch {{batch}} is signed by inspector badge 207, who is listed as authorized in the competence matrix.
evidence.whyItMatters: Release is signed by an authorized person whose competence is recorded. The release record is in order.
evidence.missedExplanation: The release signature is in order. The problem lies upstream of final inspection.
evidence.falseFindingNote: The inspector is authorized and the record is signed. This is conforming.

evidence.text: Bar stock rack slot 4 holds offcuts from material lots M-208 and M-211 under one tag that names lot M-208 only.
evidence.whyItMatters: Material must remain identified so that each batch can be traced to its material lot. Mixed offcuts break the link between batch and lot.
evidence.missedExplanation: Storage areas hold traceability evidence too. Read the tags against what is in the slot.

evidence.text: Reject trend chart for machine 3 shows rejects rising from 0.4 to 2.1 percent over four weeks. The monthly review minutes of week 11 do not mention it.
evidence.whyItMatters: Data that is collected should be analyzed and used. The chart showed a warning before the complaint. This is an opportunity to improve the review, not yet a missed requirement.
evidence.missedExplanation: Trend data often shows an issue before a customer does. Ask whether anyone reviewed it.

evidence.text: Instrument cabinet: each of the 14 instruments carries a label with its identity and due date; labels match the register.
evidence.whyItMatters: Instruments are identified so that their calibration status can be seen at the point of use.
evidence.missedExplanation: The labelling system works. The gap is in what happens when a due date passes.
evidence.falseFindingNote: Labels and the register agree. The cabinet itself is conforming.

decisions.prompt: Which work items need review before the containment meeting closes?
options: Only the ten brackets the customer reported
All of batch {{batch}}; the parts of batch {{batch2}} on pallet {{pallet}}; any parts measured with CAL-12 in the overdue window; and production from machine 3 since record NC-0193 was opened
Every part made at Meridian Works in the last year
decisions.rationale: The mixed pallet, the overdue instrument, and the open drift record each widen the affected population. The scope should follow the evidence: wide enough to include every affected item, and no wider than the evidence supports.
optionFeedback: Ten reported parts are a symptom. The evidence shows the same conditions applied to the whole batch and beyond.
This scope follows each trail of evidence: batch identity, instrument status, and the known machine problem.
The batch is affected, but the mixed pallet, the instrument, and the drift record reach further.
A scope with no link to the evidence wastes effort and delays the response to the real problem.

containment: Hold and review the identified work items, including stock at the customer
Notify the customer of the scope under review and the expected timing
correction: Re-inspect the held parts with a verified instrument; rework or dispose as authorized
cause: Revisions are not pushed to the cell and obsolete stock is not withdrawn
Calibration due dates give no alert before an instrument becomes overdue
Pack-out practice permits mixed pallets without separation labels
corrective: Revise the document release and withdrawal process so the cell receives revisions and removes obsolete copies
Add calibration due-date alerts and require separation labels on any shared pallet
effectiveness: Audit drawing revisions at the cell and overdue instruments monthly for three months, and check that no mixed pallets ship

debriefText.found: You followed the traveler to the records that matter. A records trail succeeds when each card leads to the next.
debriefText.missed: The most-missed card in this case is usually the overdue caliper, because it needs the instrument number from the traveler.
debriefText.falseFinding: A properly corrected record and a note that matches the current instruction are both conforming. Report what breaks a requirement, not what looks unusual.
